hypothesis: Prior audit inferred a ~n^2.5 retained-message-count resume cost from four confounded fixture points. The stock fixture has a uniquely pathological long unbroken assistant text token.
approach: Split cold resume into daemon create, daemon attach, TUI attach parse/reconstruct and first render; profile hot frame; independently probe large real no-compaction session and 50MiB capped toolResult fixture. Correct prior audit without deleting original measurements.
parity_notes: No product changes in this audit; every probe uses the same resume/attach protocol and exact frozen session bytes. The compacted benchmark remains valid as a common-path control, but the speed gap does not establish message-count causality.

excluded: Initial failed daemon attach probes (wire=132B, attach_messages=0) and create failures; only successful create+attach probes support split.
Prior 2.89MiB real-session snapshot is NOT interchangeable with newer 5.32MB/2717-message snapshot.
validity.notes: The old audit retained count points (135,519,1406,7259) vary text shape as well as count. perf DWARF profile placed 92% of 30s frame in pa_tui::width::str_width ASCII scanning inside markdown.rs wrap_spans_into; each emitted row re-measured and cloned the remaining ~4.3MB single-word text tail. 50x ~1MiB toolResult blobs are benign in the TUI because tool cards cap display; bytes are not sufficient for slowdown. Session parser/window remains sub-100ms from original audit. Stock suite is an adversarial monoword wrap stress case, not a representative large-session resume benchmark.

decision: RETRACTION: prior audit decision’s ~n^2.5 retained-message-count conclusion and >=2-7k threshold are FALSE. Compaction removes the 4.3MB unbroken text token, explaining the stock/compacted gap; counts merely co-vary. Keep the prior raw measurement values and mark its interpretation superseded. The compacted suite remains representative; watch it for regression while fixing wrap complexity under the stock stress case.
